newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up but banks square positions.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up but banks square positions.

text.p: The Philippine peso bounced back on Monday after banks took away the effect of the swap points on the weekend, traders said.
Monday's session, however, saw banks buy a lot of dollars from the Central Bank as banks closed their books for the end of half year's operation, traders said.
The peso closed at 26.376 to the dollar, higher than the previous close of 26.384 but slightly lower than the 26.375 rate at which it opened.
"It was a legitimate demand for dollars. Banks had to cover their shortfalls," a dealer said.
Banks had shorted the dollar after being hurt by the Central Bank's high overnight rate which was aimed at protecting the peso against speculative attacks from Thailand's financial problems.

Volume was heavy at $459.85 million, of which the Central Bank was estimated to have sold up to $246 million at the rates of 26.369, 26.37 for delivery of dollars today and at 26.376 for settlement the next day.
Traders said volume was bloated by deals for settlement today to dress up their books.
"Traditionally, at quarter end all over the world, the dollar is more expensive as banks bid up the borrowing rate ," a trader said.
Traders said the Central Bank may likely maintain its overnight borrowing rate at 15 percent on Tuesday to hold the peso.
